root_cause.text: The EROFS encoded-extent mapping logic in z_erofs_map_blocks_ext() misclassified plain extents as interlaced by checking only block alignment of map->m_pa and ignoring whether the on-disk physical length map->m_plen was block-aligned, leading z_erofs_transform_plain() to use the wrong layout and read out of bounds.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that “Only plain data whose start position and on-disk physical length are both aligned to the block size should be classified as interlaced plain extents,” and the patch changes the condition from `interlaced && !erofs_blkoff(sb, map->m_pa)` to `interlaced && !((map->m_pa | map->m_plen) & bmask)`, explicitly adding the missing alignment check on `map->m_plen`; it also notes crafted images with “plain extents with unaligned physical lengths” caused OOB read in `z_erofs_transform_plain()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a block-size mask local variable in `z_erofs_map_blocks_ext()` for later block alignment or offset calculations.
intent_record.what: A new local variable `bmask` is introduced in `z_erofs_map_blocks_ext()` and initialized to `sb->s_blocksize - 1` immediately after the `pos` calculation.
intent_record.how: At runtime this makes a block-size-derived bitmask available for subsequent logic in the function, enabling block alignment or offset masking operations using the superblock block size.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix EROFS extent mapping to mask plen flag bits before format selection and require both address and length alignment for interlaced compression detection.
intent_record.what: The code moves the checks that extract flags from map->m_plen so that the partial-reference bit is tested and EROFS_MAP_PARTIAL_REF is set, and then map->m_plen is masked with Z_EROFS_EXTENT_PLEN_MASK, before selecting m_algorithmformat. It also changes the interlaced-format condition from checking only !erofs_blkoff(sb, map->m_pa) to checking that both map->m_pa and map->m_plen are block-aligned via !((map->m_pa | map->m_plen) & bmask).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the compressed extent length is sanitized before being used in algorithm selection, and interlaced compression is now chosen only when both the physical address and payload length are block-aligned. This prevents encoded flag bits in m_plen from influencing the alignment test and avoids misclassifying extents as interlaced when their length is not properly aligned.

relevance_review.reason: The change is in z_erofs_map_blocks_ext() and introduces block-size masking used for alignment checks/calculations, which is directly tied to the root cause involving incorrect extent classification based on block alignment.

The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes encoded-extent format selection by masking plen flag bits and requires both physical address and physical length alignment before treating an extent as interlaced, preventing plain extents from being misclassified and avoiding the resulting out-of-bounds read.

candidates.rationale: This is the core misclassification check: it treats an extent as interlaced based only on physical address block alignment, without also ensuring the physical length is block-aligned, which matches the stated root cause.
This uses m_plen before masking out flag bits, contributing to incorrect format selection and interacting with the later fallback interlaced detection logic described in the fix intent.
This assignment in the interlaced branch applies the wrong layout classification once the flawed condition is satisfied, directly enabling the out-of-bounds read path in z_erofs_transform_plain().
Masking m_plen only after format selection and interlaced/plain classification means earlier logic may inspect unmasked length/flag bits, which is part of the bug fixed here.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional is the direct root cause of the misclassification: it decides an extent is interlaced by checking only that map->m_pa is block-aligned, without also requiring map->m_plen to be block-aligned. That allows plain extents to be incorrectly marked interlaced, leading later plain-transform logic to use the wrong layout and read out of bounds.

bic_trace_step.reason: The new function `z_erofs_map_blocks_ext()` contains the extent-to-layout classification logic directly, so the snippet is sufficient to judge. The vulnerable construct is present in the encoded-extent path: after loading `map->m_plen` and `map->m_pa`, the code sets `map->m_algorithmformat` using `else if (interlaced && !erofs_blkoff(sb, map->m_pa)) map->m_algorithmformat = Z_EROFS_COMPRESSION_INTERLACED; else map->m_algorithmformat = Z_EROFS_COMPRESSION_SHIFTED;`. This checks only whether `map->m_pa` is block-aligned (`!erofs_blkoff(sb, map->m_pa)`) and does not verify that the on-disk physical length `map->m_plen` is also block-aligned before treating the extent as interlaced. Per the root cause, that missing `m_plen` alignment check is exactly what misclassifies plain extents as interlaced. The code later masks the length with `map->m_plen &= Z_EROFS_EXTENT_PLEN_MASK;`, but there is still no block-alignment validation of `map->m_plen` for the interlaced decision. Therefore the bug is present, and the fix is not yet included.
